summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said out loud that it classified the task as bounded. It asked one clarifying question, then laid out both truncation approaches in chat, recommended word-boundary with a hard-cut fallback, and said "I'll hold here until you say go." After I approved, it started implementing with TDD. No spec file was written; the only repo changes are to format.js and format.test.js.
reasoning: All seven criteria have evidence from the session log and files on disk. Brainstorming was loaded first and the agent announced a bounded classification. Both alternatives were presented in chat with a recommendation, and the agent waited for approval before editing anything. No spec file exists and the only repo changes are the two source files. Implementation started with TDD right after approval.

observations.description: Before recommending an approach, the agent asked a clarifying question through AskUserQuestion: should '...' count toward maxLength? That is a different fork from the one the user asked about (exact cut vs word boundary). It was reasonable, but it added a round trip before the user's actual question got answered.

The Codex approach gate ran. Preflight returned `ok`, but the call to the stub came back empty ("the call came back empty — no approaches"). The agent handled it cleanly with no retry and said so openly. Worth checking whether an empty response from the seeded stub is expected.

The session log includes text from the hyperpowers repo's own docs/CLAUDE.md (e.g. "`docs/hyperpowers/specs/` records why a skill is shaped the way it is", "Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-22-harness-model-design.md`"). The workdir sits inside the hyperpowers repo tree, so parent-directory context appears to leak into the agent under test and could bias its behavior. Consider isolating the workdir outside the repo.
On the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs, the cursor starts on 'No, exit', so a tester has to press Down each time to continue.
The agent pointed out, without being asked, that the existing format.test.js uses console.assert, which never exits non-zero, so 'All tests passed' prints even when assertions fail. Useful catch.
Heads-up: the design picks up extra choices of its own (0 < maxLength <= 3 returns a slice of '...', and truncation is applied after prefix/suffix). Both were flagged in chat.
I pressed Escape and then /exit while the agent was mid-TDD, after it had started implementing, so the implementation was cut short on purpose. The story ends once implementation begins.

criteria.evidence: Session log: first tool call is `TOOL: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`. It came before any Edit to repo files. The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".
Assistant text: "Classification: **bounded** — `format()` already exists in `format.js` and this adds one more option inside it, so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Assistant message: "## Recommendation: word boundary, with hard-cut fallback. Straight hard-cut is only 'simpler' on paper..." It also covered and rejected a third hybrid option, and ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." In the log, all Edit calls to format.test.js/format.js come after the user message "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that".

criteria.criterion: No spec file created under docs/*/specs
criteria.evidence: `find coding-agent-workdir -path '*/docs*' -not -path '*/.git/*'` returned nothing. `git status --short` showed only ` M format.js` and ` M format.test.js`. The only Write calls in the log went to ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md, which are outside the repo. The only mentions of docs/*/specs in the log come from loaded context text, not from any Write.
`grep -io 'spike|architectural'` over the assistant text blocks returned no matches. The classification given was "bounded".

criteria.criterion: Did not classify as architectural and write a spec
criteria.evidence: Classification was "bounded". No docs/ directory exists in the workdir, and the log has no spec Write.

Assistant text after approval: "Approved — implementing. TDD applies...". It loaded Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development, then said "RED first — writing the tests before touching `format.js`", edited format.test.js, and reported "RED confirmed: 9 of the 12 new assertions fail".
